title: Cloudflare Decisions API launch: What it means
summary: The Cloudflare Decisions API launch provides developers with a programmatic way to enforce security policies across automated workflows and AI agents.
body_markdown:
## How to connect Cloudflare Decisions to an Activepieces workflow today


Activepieces converts Cloudflare's binary policy responses into enforceable administrative actions across 739+ integrations in your SaaS stack.


While Activepieces does not yet have a native Cloudflare Decisions connector, automation builders can integrate this API today using the HTTP Request integration to enforce security logic within their workflows.


Activepieces treats every agent as a managed user rather than just a script, applying the same RBAC, SSO, and SCIM policies that govern human employees.


In the run detail view, every tool call made by an agent is logged as a distinct event with its own inputs and outputs, providing the auditability required by organizations like MoneyGram and FundingSocieties.


### Option 1: Using the HTTP Request integration


Enforcing policy is most directly achieved via the HTTP Request integration, which allows Activepieces to query the Decisions API as a synchronous blocking step.


This mechanism ensures that every tool call is logged individually with its own input and output, satisfying the audit requirements for production environments at companies like Alan and Moneypenny.


Zero Trust architecture requires a "Policy Enforcement Point," and this method satisfies it. It ensures no data leaves the workflow until the Cloudflare engine validates the request context. The screenshot below illustrates this enforcement in a real-world incident response flow.


\[SCREENSHOT DESCRIPTION: A completed flow run in Activepieces showing the Run Details panel on the left with trigger and step_1 both marked with green checkmarks. The center shows a flow diagram with "Instance Stopped" trigger and "Revoke Token" step_1 connected by an arrow, both with success indicators.


The left panel displays the step_1 details including Duration (1271ms), Input showing a JSON POST request to squareup.com with Authorization header, and Output showing a JSON response with status 200 and "OK" statusText. The right panel shows the "Edit Revoke Token" configuration for an HTTP Send Request action with Method set to POST and Url field populated. A green success banner at the bottom states "Run succeeded (9e69b73e-984b-40e9-a73a-4c50382762b)".\]


The workflow proceeds with the POST request to the payment provider only because the Decisions API validated the "Revoke Token" request. If the policy engine had returned a "Deny" response, the Activepieces flow would have terminated at step_1, preventing an unauthorized credential rotation.


### Option 2: Connecting via OpenAI-compatible AI providers


For workflows involving generative agents, Activepieces can route requests through Cloudflare by configuring the OpenAI-compatible provider setting to point at a Cloudflare AI Gateway endpoint.


This setup allows the MIT-licensed core to maintain central governance over model spend and access, regardless of which provider key is used.


This configuration ensures that every prompt sent to a model such as GPT-6 Astra is logged and filtered against the Decisions API before reaching the inference server.


This setup addresses data residency and PII redaction controls by intercepting the payload at the proxy level rather than relying on the agent's internal logic.


### Option 3: Utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers


Agents can also leverage the Model Context Protocol (MCP) via Activepieces to access a standardized interface for querying corporate policy.


The same integration action that runs in a flow is exposed as an MCP tool in the open source repo under packages/integrations, allowing agents to call the Decisions API directly.


By hosting an MCP server that wraps the Decisions API, you allow frontier-class models like Gemini 3.1 Pro to "ask" for permission as a native tool-calling function.


This shifts the security model from reactive filtering to proactive compliance, where the agent checks its own proposed actions against the Cloudflare engine before attempting to execute them.
